clue.text: Striking display of energy and power during match I played

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the time span, here within the other letters
played suggests the letters of the words are performed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tennis player puts on a forceful show of stamina and strength in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striking makes a forceful, emphasised impression, the core sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Got together at social event, consuming a portion of food

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing up, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: people who met got together
a ball is a formal dance, a social event

explanation.surface: People met at a party and ate something.
explanation.definitionFit: A meatball is a single rounded serving-sized piece of minced meat, a portion of food.

clue.text: Sportsman despondent after forty-five minutes of play?

indicators.note: after puts the despondent word behind the first piece

parts.note: a football match half lasts forty-five minutes
blue means sad or low in spirits

explanation.surface: A footballer feeling down at half-time.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge, a half blue is an award for representing the university in a minor sport, and so names the sportsman holding it.

clue.text: Working animals regularly deployed in the farm

indicators.note: regularly deployed means using every other letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Draught animals are put to use all over the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is a group of animals such as oxen or horses harnessed together to pull a load.

clue.text: Language spoken during procedure at airport

indicators.note: spoken says the language's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Czech is the language of the Czech Republic
in means during, as in 'in the night'

explanation.surface: A foreign tongue is used during airport formalities.
explanation.definitionFit: Check-in is the airport desk procedure where travellers register and drop off luggage before boarding.

clue.text: Love knitted sweater fellow's wearing on top of T-shirt

indicators.note: wearing means the fellow goes inside, enclosed like a body in a garment
knitted suggests the letters of sweater are worked into a new pattern

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a fellow; the possessive is 'fellow is'

indicators.note: top of means only the opening letter of the garment word is used

explanation.surface: My darling's woolly sweater is pulled on over his T-shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knitted' rearranges the jumper's letters, and 'wearing' sets the fellow inside them, as a person inside a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Love used as an endearment is a pet name for a beloved, as is the word for a darling partner.

clue.text: Writer's very bad, getting in endless fighting

definitions.note: the 's is 'is': the writer is the answer

indicators.note: getting in means the pieces enter the other word
endless means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a melee is a confused scrimmage of fighting
ill can mean bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: An author is terribly poor, caught up in a never-ending brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of the brawl word, and 'getting in' sets the very-bad pieces inside it. A melee is a confused fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Herman Melville was the American novelist of Moby-Dick, a writer.

clue.text: Indeed, Conservative has high opinion of old philosopher

parts.note: so can mean indeed, as in 'it is so'
C abbreviates Conservative in British politics
rates means thinks highly of

explanation.surface: A Tory thinks well of an ancient thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the Athenian thinker of the fifth century BC, the founder of Western philosophy.

clue.text: Awkward situation makes wife change colour in middle of house party

indicators.note: in middle of puts the wife and colour change inside the other pieces

parts.note: a do is a party
to dye is to change a colour

explanation.surface: At a house party a wife's hair dye goes wrong, causing embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: A how-d'ye-do is an old idiom for an awkward fix or muddle, a fine mess.

clue.text: Spot trouble lurking within fast-flowing stretch of water

indicators.note: lurking within means the trouble is concealed inside the other word

parts.note: to trace is to find or spot
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Danger hidden in a swift river current.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailrace is the channel carrying water swiftly away from a mill wheel or turbine.

clue.text: Think about taking cut in insurance

indicators.note: taking means the insurance word takes in the other piece

parts.note: cover is insurance protection
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: Ponder whether to reduce your insurance.
explanation.definitionFit: To chew over an idea is an idiom for mulling it, as one would chew food slowly.

clue.text: Application giving digitally-enhanced results

parts.note: reads like software that edits photos, but digits are fingers, and an application is something put on

explanation.definitionFit: Varnish applied to fingernails makes the digits look better, an application with digital results.

clue.text: Air-traffic controller's final words about flyer heading off

parts.note: over means about, concerning, as in a row over money

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a handout is a printed flyer or leaflet

explanation.surface: A tower controller signs off as a plane departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyer' suggests an aircraft, but it is a leaflet; 'heading off' strips its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio users sign off with this phrase meaning the message is ended and no reply is expected.

clue.text: Plan garden area

definitions.meaning: a small piece of ground for growing things

explanation.surface: Lay out a design for a patch of garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a scheme and a small marked-out piece of land.

clue.text: One out to provide on-line support?

definitions.text: One out to provide on-line support?

parts.words: One out to provide on-line support?
parts.note: one out is someone asleep; on-line support is what holds up railway track

explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is one out cold, and also the timber beam beneath railway rails.

clue.text: Garments bound to be seen on workers

parts.note: to bound is to leap or skip
worker ants are the crossword's usual workers

explanation.surface: Clothes certain to be spotted on employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to be seen' reads as 'certain to appear', but bound is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski pants are trousers worn for skiing, so items of clothing.

clue.text: Spent very little money after former partner died

indicators.note: after sends the money and death pieces behind the former partner

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
P is a penny, a tiny sum
ended means died, came to an end

explanation.surface: A divorcee who has passed away left almost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Expended is a formal synonym of spent, as money or effort used up.

clue.text: Country's leaders risk sea battles

indicators.note: battles suggests the letters fighting their way into a new order

explanation.surface: National rulers gamble on naval warfare.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaisers were the German emperors, rulers of their nation.

clue.text: Dotty old actor took the lead following shaky start

indicators.note: following means the actor and lead come after the opening letter
start means the first letter of shaky

parts.note: Gregory Peck was a Hollywood film star
led means took the lead

explanation.surface: A doddery old thespian headed the cast after a wobbly opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotty in its literal sense means covered in dots, which is what speckled describes.

clue.text: Playfellow lost in regatta out east

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters are scattered and mixed up
out means the following letter is removed

explanation.surface: A playmate goes missing at a boat race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E (east) from REGATTA, and 'lost' shuffles IN plus RGATTA. 'Playfellow' reads as a playmate, but it is a fellow who writes plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan was an English dramatist, a fellow known for his plays.

clue.text: Wearing clothes makes you hot when sleeping, it's maintained

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

indicators.note: maintained means held, so the sleeping word holds the other

parts.note: abed means in bed, sleeping
it with 's for 'is': it is held

explanation.surface: Sleeping in pyjamas makes you warm, it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: Habited is an old word meaning dressed, especially in a monk's or nun's habit.

clue.text: Is no skill needed in party game?

indicators.note: no means the skill word is absent from the party

parts.note: art is a skill

explanation.surface: A simple children's party game needs no special ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes ART (skill) out of PARTY, leaving PY.
explanation.definitionFit: I-spy is a guessing game played by children, naming objects by their initial letter.

clue.text: Separate soldiers in tanks initially missing civilian accommodation?

indicators.note: in places the separate soldiers inside the tanks word
initially missing means the first letter of the tanks word is lost

parts.note: vats are large tanks for liquid
to part is to separate
men are soldiers, the other ranks

explanation.surface: Isolate the troops in their armoured vehicles, with no barracks for non-military people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially missing' drops the tanks word's first letter; 'in' places the separating soldiers inside. The question mark flags that apartments house civilians, unlike barracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartments are flats, homes for ordinary people rather than military quarters.

clue.text: Choral piece that is performed about beginning of day —— a round

indicators.note: round means the whole string is turned back to front
about means the first two pieces go around the opening letter of day

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
sung means performed by singers

indicators.note: beginning of means the first letter of day

explanation.surface: A choir sings a canon at the start of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts D inside IESUNG, giving IEDSUNG; add A, then 'round' turns the whole string back to front. The dash makes 'a round' look like a canon, the choral form.
explanation.definitionFit: The Agnus Dei is a section of the Mass often set to music for choir.

clue.text: Part of Europe not accessible

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A region of the continent that cannot be reached.
explanation.definitionFit: Open means available or approachable, as an accessible place or person is.

clue.text: Study of local area as explorer got back round furthest part of Germany

indicators.note: round means the reversed word goes around the explorer
back means the word got is read backwards

parts.note: Marco Polo was the Venetian traveller to China

indicators.note: furthest part of means the last letter of Germany

explanation.surface: An explorer surveyed a district far into German territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Topology in an older sense is the detailed study of a particular place's features.

clue.text: Start to think about getting a safe for valuable objects

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of think

parts.note: re means about, concerning
sure means safe, as in 'a sure bet'

explanation.surface: Consider buying a strongbox for one's jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is a hoard of precious things such as gold and jewels.

clue.text: Fight indicated by sound of bell

definitions.meaning: the chime of a bell is imitated as ...

explanation.surface: A boxing bout signalled by the ringing bell.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for a lively quarrel and also the echoic word for a bell's chime.
